title: Universality of the $1/9$ Magnetization Plateau and Quantum-Disordered States in the Kagome Family $\mathrm{Cs_8AB_3Ti_{12}F_{48}}$ ($A=\mathrm{Rb},\mathrm{Li}$; $B=\mathrm{K},\mathrm{Na}$)
authors: Prena Chaudhary, Asiri Thennakoon, Tommy Park, Hanru Wang, Leshan Zhao, Laurel Winter, Neil Herrison, Christina Hoffmann, Junghong H. He, Harald O. Jeschke, Hiroyuki Nojiri, Akira Matsuo, Koichi Kindo, Miwako Takahashi, Yukio Noda, Taku J. Sato, Shiyan Li, Hiroaki Ueda, Gia-Wei Chern, Seung-Hun Lee
abstract: The microscopic origin of the low-field $1/9$ magnetization plateau in spin-$1/2$ kagome antiferromagnets remains unresolved. Here, we show that chemical pressure reshapes the hierarchy of fractional magnetization plateaus in the titanium-based kagome family $\mathrm{Cs_8AB_3Ti_{12}F_{48}}$ ($A=\mathrm{Rb},\mathrm{Li}$; $B=\mathrm{K},\mathrm{Na}$). High-field magnetization measurements up to 60 T reveal a robust $1/9$ plateau-like phase in the expanded $\mathrm{Cs_8RbK_3Ti_{12}F_{48}}$ and $\mathrm{Cs_8LiK_3Ti_{12}F_{48}}$ compounds, despite the absence of the conventionally more robust $1/3$ plateau. In contrast, compressed $\mathrm{Cs_8LiNa_3Ti_{12}F_{48}}$ exhibits neither the $1/9$ plateau-like phase nor a quantum-disordered ground state. Specific-heat measurements and first-principles calculations show that lattice expansion preserves a frustrated, fully connected kagome exchange network and gapless quantum-disordered ground states, whereas compression reorganizes the exchange network into weakly coupled quasi-one-dimensional subsystems and induces successive magnetic transitions. These results demonstrate that the $1/9$ and $1/3$ plateaus need not share a common microscopic origin and suggest that the $1/9$ plateau may represent a more universal feature of frustrated spin-$1/2$ kagome magnetism.
summary: This study investigates how structural tuning, achieved by chemical pressure in the Kagome material Cs_8AB_3Ti_12F_48, affects magnetic ordering. By comparing expanded and compressed compounds, the researchers found that the 1/9 magnetization plateau persists robustly in expanded systems, suggesting it is a fundamental feature of frustrated kagome magnetism, independent of the more common 1/3 plateau.
main_problem: The study aims to resolve the microscopic origin and universality of the low-field 1/9 magnetization plateau in spin-1/2 kagome antiferromagnets.
main_result: The 1/9 plateau is robustly observed in expanded compounds even when the conventional 1/3 plateau is absent, suggesting the 1/9 feature may be a more universal characteristic of frustrated kagome magnetism.
method: The research combines high-field magnetization measurements, specific-heat measurements, and first-principles DFT calculations, supplemented by structural refinement using neutron and X-ray diffraction.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Kagome family of compounds, Cs_8AB_3Ti_12F_48, which are spin-1/2 antiferromagnets whose magnetic interactions are modeled by a Heisenberg Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Magnetization plateaus (1/9 and 1/3), specific heat anomalies, and derived magnetic exchange constants (J_i).
important_parameters: Chemical pressure tuning via alkali ion substitution (lattice expansion vs. compression) and high magnetic fields up to 60 T.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that structural changes (compression/expansion) directly modify the magnetic exchange network, and that the magnetic behavior can be mapped onto a Heisenberg model.
figures_summary: Figures show structural refinements and polyhedral representations; magnetization curves illustrate the emergence of the 1/9 plateau in expanded samples; specific heat data contrast the behavior of compressed versus expanded compounds.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the structural basis via joint X-ray/neutron refinement, then using DFT to map exchange interactions, and finally presenting high-field magnetization and specific heat measurements to correlate structural tuning with the magnetic plateau phases.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed experimental and computational study of geometric frustration in a solid-state magnetic system, directly addressing the emergence of fractional magnetization plateaus, which is central to understanding quantum magnetic ground states.
